data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 3d696176f68b8a4f08032d05405986d774948c95
* **observed_on:** PR #132 (https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/132) — fix branch fix/7d25-c78e-onboarding-shim-dispatch
* **components:** plugins/dso/scripts/ci-llm-review-runner.sh, plugins/dso/scripts/mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh, llm-review GitHub Actions workflow

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

When the CI llm-review job emits a finding (any severity, including 'fragile'), the finding should appear as a standard PR review comment on the relevant file/line so that:

1. The author/agent can respond inline, mark resolved, or push a defense commit per the standard PR-comment workflow.
2. The PR's review-thread API (gh pr view --json reviewThreads, gh api .../pulls/<n>/comments) returns the finding alongside other reviewer comments.
3. The finding is visible to /dso:respond-to-pr-comments and similar tooling that iterates unresolved review threads.

#### Actual Behavior

The fragile finding for PR #132 was posted by github-actions[bot] as a comment on the file/line via the pulls/<n>/comments endpoint — so it IS visible to tooling that queries that endpoint. However:

- It does NOT appear as a structured 'review thread' (gh pr view 132 --json reviewThreads returns empty) — meaning the standard 'pending review with N comments' UX doesn't fire and the comment cannot be 'resolved' through the GitHub PR review-thread UI in the same way that a Copilot review or human reviewer comment can be.
- The mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh path appears to NOT promote fragile findings into the resolvable-thread workflow that other findings (critical/important) follow.
- merge-to-main.sh's resolve_phase, which iterates unresolved review threads, never sees the fragile finding — so the PR-merge pipeline does not attempt autonomous resolution or defense for fragile findings, leaving them as a CI failure with no actionable surface other than direct file edits + force-push.

This is a UX + workflow gap: the finding exists, is rendered in the PR conversation timeline, but is not first-class in the review-thread workflow that the rest of the DSO PR pipeline operates on.

### 3. Action History

PR #132 (this session): llm-review CI step FAILED with the fragile finding visible only via pulls/.../comments endpoint. Two Copilot findings on the same PR appeared as proper review threads. The fragile finding required manual investigation via gh api to discover.

### 4. Reproduction Steps

1. Open a PR that triggers the llm-review CI job.
2. If the CI emits a fragile-severity finding (e.g., 'cannot verify external script behavior from diff'), observe:
   - gh pr view <n> --json reviewThreads returns the Copilot threads but not the fragile-finding thread.
   - gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>/comments DOES return the fragile finding (posted by github-actions[bot]).
3. Note that merge-to-main.sh resolve_phase does not iterate the fragile finding because it scans review threads, not the lower-level comments endpoint.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* plugins/dso/scripts/ci-llm-review-runner.sh — emits findings to PR
* plugins/dso/scripts/mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh — mirrors defenses
* plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main.sh — resolve_phase scans review threads
* /dso:respond-to-pr-comments — should classify/respond to ALL unresolved findings, currently misses fragile

### 6. Suggested Investigation

1. Identify which mirror path posts fragile findings vs. critical/important findings (look at ci-llm-review-runner.sh and mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh).
2. Determine whether the fix is to elevate fragile findings to review-thread comments (review_comment_request via the reviews endpoint, not just the comments endpoint), or to extend resolve_phase to also iterate the comments endpoint.
3. Either fix should preserve the existing Copilot/human review-thread behavior — only the fragile-finding posting path needs adjustment.

### Why this matters (P2)
- merge-to-main + /dso:respond-to-pr-comments treat review threads as the canonical 'unresolved feedback' surface; fragile findings are silently outside that surface.
- For autonomous PR pipelines (debug-everything, sprint), this means CI failure with no actionable feedback loop unless the orchestrator manually queries the lower-level comments endpoint.
- Discovered while addressing PR #132 review feedback — the fragile finding was almost missed because the standard PR-thread query returned empty.
data.title: [ci-llm-review/PR-comment-mirror]: 'fragile' findings from llm-review not surfaced as standard PR review comments -> blocked PR with no actionable per-file feedback
